(a) The findings of acquittal recorded by the Special Judge in the para of 81A, 82A,
83Am 84A, 85 and 86 of the impugned judgment are without appreciation of evidence.

(b) The audit report conducted by Shri Bilodiya regarding the huge transaction of amount through account opened in the Transport Cooperative Banck, Indore operated by the respondent No.4 has not been controverted and the fact that the transaction through account No.008 were not mentioned in the cash book of Housing Society.
There is no material denial in the cross examination of the witness (PW-1) and this fact has been ignored by the Trial Court while acquitting the respondents.
(c) The respondent No.3 was not member of the Housing Cooperative Society and amount of Rs.2 Crore was transferred in the account of respondent No.3.
This fact has been ignored by the Trial Court.

(d) The transaction through account No.008 were not included in the cash book, this fact has also not been reverted and the Trial Court recording the findings without considering this fact.
(e) The violation of KYC guidelines as stated by the Bherulal (PW-13) in opening the account has not been reverted and the Trial Court recorded the findings of acquittal ignoring this fact.
(f) The amount of Rs.80.79 lakhs deposited in the account No.24 opened in the Transport Cooperative Bank, Indore and during the short period the amount was withdrawn through self cheque by the respondent No.4 without intimating the FIU,
India.
This fact has not been reverted and the Trial Court recorded the findings of acquittal ignoring this fact.

(g) The account No.1002019000008 was opened on 01.01.2008 in which the identity documents were used that were previously used in account No.24 and amount of Rs.470.70 lakhs was deposited during the period of 07.01.2008 to 02.06.2008 and from this account between the period from 07.01.2008 to 02.06.2008, the amount was transferred in the saving bank account No.2540 of respondent No.3 and transaction was not intimated to FIU, India and accounts were opened after the respondent No.3 was elected as President of Board of Governors and the Trial Court recorded the findings ignoring this evidence.

(h). The Trial Court has also recorded the findings that the respondent No.4 being Manager of Housing Society has not been proved to be public servant and no sanction for prosecution under Section 19 of Prevention of Corruption Act has been obtained against the respondent No.4.

It is also argued that the findings of Trial Court not holding to public servant to the respondent No.4 is contrary to law in light of Section 87 of M.P. Co-Operative Societies Act, 1960 read with section 2 (c)

It is further submitted that apart from charges under Prevention of Corruption Act, the concerned will be liable to be prosecuted under Indian Penal Code framed against him.
8. Counsel for the respondents argued that the findings of the Trial Court is based on proper appreciation of evidence and no case for permission to leave to appeal is made out.
We have perused the impugned judgment alongwith record of the Trial Court.

9. The Trial Court recorded the findings of acquittal assigning that if intimation of huge transaction is not sent to FIU, India then concerned account holder or concerned institute have not responsbility and there was no irregularity in opening the acount No.0024 and 008.

The amount transferred from the account No.008 to the tune of Rs.2,50,08,000/- to respondent No.3 was in connection with sale agreement Ex.P/6 dated 04.01.2008 relating to the scheme for construction of multi story building on the land situated at village Bijalpur survey No.25/1/2 area 0.35 hectare or 15250 sqft. in the form of 45000 sqft. and agreement dated 03.04.2008 Ex. P/7 on the same land was executed as Ex.P/6 as the agreement Ex.P/6 was cancelled on 10.02.2008 and amount of Rs.1,90,08,00/- was returned by the respondent No.3 to the Society in the installment that was entered into back off of Ex.P/6.

The receipt Ex.P/19 was also executed by the respondent No.4 in favour of the respondent No.3 and Rs.60 lakhs were returned to the Society upto 11.05.2009 and receipt dated 12.05.2009 Ex.P/20 was executed by the respondent No.4 and that was also mentioned page No.1 of Ex.P/7.

The receipts Ex.P/8 to Ex.P/18 were also executed that were entered into ledger book of respondent No.3 adduced as Ex.P/22 to Ex.P/25 and found that Ex.P.6 and P/7 are reliable and also referred to the audit report Ex.D/2.

The principle to be considered at the time of considering the application under Section 378(3)
of the Cr.P.C have been dealt with in State of Maharashtra Vs. Sujay Mangesh Poyarelar AIR 2008 (9) SCC 475, the relevant para 27 is reproduced as below:-
"We may hasten to clarify that we may not be understood to have laid down an inviolable rule that no leave should be refused by the appellate Court against an order of acquittal recorded by the trial Court.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra Vs. Sujay Mangesh Poyarelar AIR 2008 (9) SCC 475
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We only state that in such cases, the appellate Court must consider the relevant material, sworn testimonies of prosecution witnesses and record reasons why leave sought by the State should not be granted and the order of acquittal recorded by the trial Court should not be disturbed.
Where there is application of mind by the appellate Court and reasons (may be in brief) in support of such view are recorded, the order of the Court may not be said to be illegal or objectionable.

At the same time, however, if arguable points have been raised, if the material on record discloses deeper scrutiny and re-appreciation, review or reconsideration of evidence, the appellate Court must grant leave as sought and decide the appeal on merits."

sentences.text: Considered that after execution of agreement dated 04.01.2008 (Ex.P/6) another agreement (Ex.P/7) was executed regarding the same land.

The amount of Rs. 2 crores was transferred to the account of Housing Society in favour of respondent No.3 by respondent No.4 and no agreement was honoured and so called return of amount was through cash regarding which the respondents No.4 executed receipts.

12. Looking to the findings of acquittal recorded by the Trial Court, evidence as available on record and grounds raised for permission to leave to appeal, arguable points arises and the material on record discloses the deeper scrutiny and re-appreciation of evidence.
Accordingly, it is a fit case to grant the leave to appeal under Section 378(3) of the Cr.
P.C. Office is directed to issue Bailable Warrants of Rs.50,000/- against the respondents.

13. The respondents are directed to furnish a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with separate solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for their appearance before this registry on 14.10.2024 and on subsequent dated as maybe fixed by this registry.

14. List the matter for final hearing in due course.
